extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings (Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, USPTO Director)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules the USPTO applies when deciding whether to impose reciprocal discipline based on a state's disciplinary adjudication under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24. Covers the evidentiary burden, the Selling v. Radford factors, sanction identity, probation enforcement, and notice/publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: A state disciplinary adjudication creates a federal-level presumption that imposition of reciprocal discipline is proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Selling v. Radford, the USPTO presumes reciprocal discipline appropriate unless the respondent clearly and convincingly demonstrates one of the enumerated exceptions (due process defect, infirmity of proof, grave injustice, or that no public discipline occurred). The USPTO (like federal courts) is not acting as a court of review to relitigate state findings; the presumption is strong and narrow standards for overcoming it are applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identical sanction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director shall impose the identical public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension, or disciplinary disqualification unless an exception is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office implements the same form and level of discipline imposed by the state unless a clear-and-convincing showing of a Selling factor justifies deviation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selling factor — deprivation of due process (notice/opportunity to be heard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent may avoid reciprocal discipline by showing the state procedure was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute deprivation of due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To succeed the respondent must present clear and convincing evidence of the procedural defect. Mere disagreement with the state process is insufficient; factual proof that notice or hearing was constitutionally or procedurally deficient is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selling factor — infirmity of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent may avoid reciprocal discipline by showing there was such infirmity of proof establishing the conduct as to give rise to the clear conviction that the USPTO could not accept the state conclusion as final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires clear and convincing evidence that the state record is so deficient that the Office cannot, consistently with its duty, accept the state finding. The standard is narrow; courts have stressed deference to the initial adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selling factor — grave injustice
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent may avoid reciprocal discipline by showing that imposition of the same discipline by the USPTO would result in a grave injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grave injustice analysis focuses on whether the severity of the punishment 'fits' the misconduct (i.e., whether the sanction is so ill-fitted that imposing it would be fundamentally unfair). Evidence that the state already considered mitigating factors (e.g., illness) weighs against a grave injustice claim. The respondent must prove grave injustice by clear and convincing evidence; cited cases illustrate that sanctions within the state’s usual range are not a grave injustice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selling factor — that no public discipline occurred
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent may argue the practitioner was not publicly censured, publicly reprimanded, placed on probation, disbarred, suspended, or disciplinarily disqualified as a basis to avoid reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative factual challenge to whether the state actually imposed the alleged public discipline; clear documentary evidence would be required to rebut the state judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's burden and standard of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent bears the burden to demonstrate, by clear and convincing evidence, that one of the Selling elements applies to preclude reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal precedent treats this burden narrowly; the Office will not relitigate state findings and will require strong proof (clear and convincing) to find a genuine issue of material fact that avoids identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of inquiry — not a court of review
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's review in a reciprocal-discipline proceeding is limited and not intended to be a de novo review of the state adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will generally accept the state court's factual and legal conclusions unless the respondent can clearly and convincingly establish one of the narrow exceptions. Citations (e.g., In re Zdravkovich, In re Sibley) emphasize deference to the original proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of state mitigation in grave-injustice claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating factors considered by the state (e.g., physical or mental illness) are part of the state record and generally undercut claims that reciprocal discipline would be a grave injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the state proceeding already considered and accounted for mitigation in setting the sanction, claiming that such mitigation warrants avoiding identical discipline before the USPTO is unlikely to succeed unless new, clear-and-convincing evidence shows otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation enforcement procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural steps for addressing alleged noncompliance with probation terms during the USPTO-ordered probationary period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the OED Director believes the respondent failed to comply with the Final Order during probation, the OED Director shall: (1) issue an Order to Show Cause, (2) send it to respondent's last address of record per 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a), and (3) grant respondent 15 days to respond. If after considering any response the OED Director still believes noncompliance occurred, the OED Director shall deliver the Order to Show Cause, respondent's response (if any), and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for the failure to comply. Any review of an ensuing USPTO Director order will not stay the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to publicize the discipline and notify relevant agencies/venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director must publish a Notice of Reprimand and Probation in the Official Gazette and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is admitted, and to the public. Disciplinary decisions are made available in the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of conduct supporting discipline (examples of misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific ethical violations alleged/found in the underlying state proceeding that support discipline (fees, termination, meritorious claims, respect for rights, misconduct prejudicial to administration of justice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Arizona decision identified violations of ER 1.5 (Fees), ER 1.16 (Termination of Representation), ER 3.1 (Meritorious Claims and Contentions), ER 4.4 (Respect for the Rights of Others), and ER 8.4(d) (Misconduct Prejudicial to the Administration of Justice). The Final Order summarizes factual examples: failing to promptly return a client's file and inappropriate billing practices (including billing time to 'wait and see' if opposing counsel filed documents). Such factual findings in the state record support imposition of reciprocal discipline absent successful Selling challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The legal basis authorizing USPTO action on reciprocal discipline matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59. These provisions authorize the Office to impose discipline and to publish/notify regarding disciplinary actions; they set the regulatory framework applied in the Final Order.
